subject: SLA redlines: multi-region uptime banding & maintenance blackout proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@orchid.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai; procurement@orchid.ai
Cc: tim.cho@orchid.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood MSA/Order Form — SLA redlines

Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement and infra have a couple of ask items that we need reflected in the Order Form / SLA before legal will sign:

1) Uptime target: we need a 99.95% weighted availability across our multi-region deployment (primary + failover).
2) Service credit scale: credits should escalate to 50% of monthly fees at <=99.5% availability and be pro-rated across regions based on customer impact.
3) Response times: P1 15 minutes, P2 2 hours, P3 8 hours — these are gating for our incident playbooks.
4) Maintenance windows: we need a 4-hour weekly maintenance blackout to be clearly defined (and a clause for no unscheduled maintenance in our US production region during business hours).

Attached is a redline our procurement team started. Please advise what is acceptable and what requires separate approval. We are on a tight calendar — aiming to execute the order form by end of month.

Appreciate a quick sync,
Sarah
Senior Procurement Manager
Orchid Analytics

Attachments: Orchid_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@orchid.ai>, procurement@orchid.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 11:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — SLA redlines

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. High level response: we absolutely want to get you the right guarantees for production-critical workloads, but a few of these items have trade-offs that require coordination across legal and ops.

Quick notes:
- Uptime: 99.95% is above our standard hosted Availability Tier for the committed SKU you selected. We can offer a 99.95% SLO as a paid addendum on Dedicated fleets or a fixed price uplift for hosted with a regional failover requirement.
- Credits: We can structure pro-rated credits by region and agree a staircase up to 40% of monthly fees for a combined availability <99.5% rather than 50% — this reduces counterparty exposure and aligns with our risk models.
- Response SLAs: P1 15m is tight for our global rotation; we can commit to 30m P1 for hosted and 15m for Dedicated with a named primary contact and 24/7 escalation.
- Maintenance: we can accept a blackout clause for in-business-hour restrictions in US primary region for emergency maintenance, and propose a rolling weekly maintenance window up to 6 hours outside business hours for non-critical upgrades.

Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (ops) — Laura / Ben, any legal/ops constraints I should flag back to Sarah? If you confirm, I will send an updated redline (OrderForm_v3) and schedule a 30-min sync.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_ORCH_v3_redline.docx (will circulate after legal confirmation)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@orchid.ai>, procurement@orchid.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — SLA redlines

Jonas / Sarah — some quick legal points on the proposed changes:

- Uptime change: shifting to a 99.95% contractual availability is acceptable as long as the definition of "availability" explicitly excludes customer-caused outage (misconfiguration) and connections outside our network boundary. We will add precise metric definitions (window granularity, sample rate, percent-of-interval calculation).
- Credit cap: legal comfortable with a 40% cap; if procurement insists on 50%, we need exec approval and a corresponding indemnity/limitation adjustment.
- Retroactivity and lookback: do not accept retroactive credits more than one billing period. We will add a clause limiting credit claims to 60 days post-incident to control exposure.
- Emergency maintenance carveout: add a requirement to provide 72-hour prior notice where practicable and an incident report within 5 business days after emergency maintenance.

I'll draft redline language for the definitions and credit staircase. Jonas — if Orchid pushes 50%, escalate to Marissa for final approval.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@orchid.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 14:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — SLA redlines

Ops perspective: a couple of operational constraints and an alternative suggestion.

1) Measurement granularity: we measure region availability at 1-minute resolution and calculate monthly availability using calendar month totals. We should include that explicitly to avoid ambiguity.
2) Multi-region pro-rating: implementing per-region pro-rated credits requires per-customer telemetry partitioning and will add ~2-3 weeks to provisioning. If Orchid needs that on day one, we should plan for a one-time implementation fee.
3) Maintenance windows: our standard weekly maintenance is 6 hours in the 0200-0600 UTC window to cover rolling updates. To meet Orchid's in-business-hours restriction in US primary, we recommend a scheduled weekly 2-hour window in US-PST late evening plus emergency maintenance carveouts only for critical CVEs (with a defined approval channel).

Operational ask: if Orchid accepts the 40% max credit staircase and acknowledges the one-time implementation effort for per-region pro-rating, we can commit to 99.95% on Dedicated or offer a 99.90% across hosted with clearly documented regional failover.

Ben Carter
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@orchid.ai>, procurement@orchid.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 16:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA/Order Form — SLA redlines (next steps)

Sarah — thanks for the patience and the good discussion. Summary and proposed next steps: 

Agreed commercial positions:
- Availability: Redwood to provide 99.95% contractual SLO for Orchid if customer elects Dedicated capacity (Order Form addendum). If customer remains on hosted, Redwood will provide 99.90% with documented cross-region failover behavior.
- Credit staircase: agree to a pro-rated regional credit model capped at 40% monthly fees; Orchid may request 50% which requires Marissa's sign-off and a corresponding legal/limitation clause adjustment.
- Response times: commit to P1 15m for Dedicated (named escalation) and P1 30m for hosted; P2/P3 as proposed (2h/8h) for both.
- Maintenance: Redwood to restrict non-emergency maintenance in US primary during business hours and schedule a weekly 2-hour local maintenance window plus a 6-hour global window outside business hours for other updates. Emergency maintenance carveouts allowed with 72-hour notice when practicable and post-event report within 5 business days.

Operational / implementation notes:
- Per-region credit pro-rating will incur a one-time setup fee (ops estimate included in the attached OrderForm_ORCH_v3_redline.docx).
- Measurement definition: availability measured at 1-minute resolution, monthly calendar aggregation.

Next steps:
1) Laura will circulate the legal redline language today (she's on copy).
2) I will attach OrderForm_v3 with the commercial positions and a DocuSign envelope once Laura calls out any final open legal language.
3) If Orchid insists on 50% cap, I'll escalate to Marissa for commercial sign-off.

Please confirm you are ok with these positions and I will send the updated doc and DocuSign link.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quarter.
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
